question: [PRACTICE] What will the average "new forecasters per day" be on this question before this question closes?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: FutureEval/AI-Benchmark season warm-up practice questions, rate = forecasters at close / days open. The one cited instance (Summer 2026 practice question, 156 forecasters) gives a class anchor near 6.5/day if its window matched the ~17-18 day announcement-to-start gap seen in both prior seasons, or near 5.5 over a ~4-week window. I shade below that anchor for two reasons: this is a discrete question, and discrete/numeric formats reliably draw fewer bots than the flagship binary the 156 figure comes from; and the window may be longer than the announcement gap if the practice batch was created before the public announcement. Evidence is thin and one-sided in an unusual way - I could confirm the season calendar from two EA Forum announcements but could not open the Metaculus question page or API (403 / auth-gated), so I never saw this question's actual open date or current forecaster count. That missing denominator is most of my spread. No human prediction market prices this. Upper escape (>10.05/day) is priced at 7% on a concrete mechanism: a short ~19-day window combined with Fall-season participation growth pushing past ~190 forecasters. Lower escape (<0.95/day) at 3% would need either a much longer window than any prior warm-up or near-total bot absence on a discrete question, both hard to reconcile with 156 on the sibling question.

calls.reasoning: Reference class: Metaculus FutureEval seasonal bot-tournament practice/warm-up questions, forecasters at close divided by days open. The Summer 2026 analog (q43339) drew 156 forecasters and appears to have run ~17-18 days from the ~May 1 announcement to the May 18 season start, implying roughly 8-9/day; taking a looser ~150 forecasters over a ~25-day warm-up gives ~6, so I anchor the class near 6.5/day. Two adjustments pull down: this is a discrete, self-referential, unusual-format post, and in the Summer batch numeric/discrete questions drew 80-129 forecasters versus 137-180 for binaries, so the numerator likely lands below the 156 quoted in the background; and this window looks longer (~22 days, open after Sep 3 per the repo's API note, closing Sep 28) than Summer's, which enlarges the denominator. Pulling up: the bot field has grown season over season, and warm-up traffic concentrates in the final week before a season start, so most of the eventual count is still ahead. Net: a median near 5.3/day (~117 forecasters over ~22 days), with wide bands because the numerator is the dominant unknown. Escape mass: 2% below 0.95 (would need under ~21 total forecasters - the twin post already has 14, so this needs near-total neglect) and 6% above 10.05 (needs ~220+ forecasters, achievable only with a much larger Fall bot field than any prior season plus a shorter-than-assumed open window). No prediction market prices this; none found on Polymarket, Kalshi, or Manifold.

calls.reasoning: Resolution is (forecasters in the Metaculus UI at close) / (days open). Post-ID adjacency (45316 = Aug-24 MiniBench wave, 45534/45544 = Sep-7 wave) puts the open date ~Sep 5-6, so the denominator is ~22-23 days; the UI currently shows 14 forecasters, i.e. ~3.2/day over the first ~4.4 days. Reference class: FutureEval warm-up/testing-area questions, whose lifetime averages run ~1.4/day (EU warm-up: 180 forecasters since ~May) but which accrue much faster during a season launch - that same question went 156 -> 180 in the days since this question was authored, implying ~3/day of new-bot arrivals right now. The Fall 2026 tournament has not started (page lists no questions; scaffold prep notes say the Fall slug was absent from the projects API on 2026-09-03, expected ~mid-September), so the largest single driver - a launch wave of 100-160 returning bots polling the seasonal slug and picking up the warm-up - falls inside the remaining 18 days if the question is carried in the tournament project (its card shows 'Bot testing area' + 1 more). Main counterargument: arrivals to a fresh question are front-loaded and then decay, and if this stays testing-area-only or the Fall slug opens near Sep 21, the final count could stall near 40-60, i.e. ~2/day. I therefore centre near 4.2 with a long right tail toward the 150-190 counts seen on MiniBench and the Summer warm-up.

calls.reference_class: Metaculus FutureEval bot warm-up / bot-testing-area practice questions, measured as forecasters accrued divided by days open, restricted to windows overlapping a season launch

calls.reasoning: This post is the Fall practice copy closing at the Sep 28 season start, not the 14-forecaster testing-area twin that runs to 2028 - so the Summer analog's 156-at-close is the right anchor, giving ~6.5/day before adjustment. Two adjustments pull down: this is a discrete question, and the Summer batch shows discrete drawing ~80 vs ~180 for the binary (bots skip or error on non-binary formats), so the numerator likely lands near 90-115; and the window looks like ~22-23 days (post-ID adjacency puts the open ~Sep 5-6), longer than Summer's announcement-to-start gap. Pulling up: the bot field has grown season over season (267 Summer entrants) and warm-up traffic concentrates in the final week before a season start, so most of the count is still ahead of Now. Median 4.8/day (~105 forecasters over 22 days); bands are wide because neither the open date nor the current count could be verified - Metaculus returned 403/auth-gated to all three runs. Escape mass: 6% above 10.05 (needs ~200+ forecasters on a shorter-than-assumed window) and 3% below 0.95 (needs near-total neglect, under ~21 forecasters, which the twin's 14 in ~4 days already argues against).
calls.reconciliation: Two factual disputes drove the spread. (1) Whether q45517 - 14 forecasters, rendered close Sep 5 2028 - is this question. Settled against Run 3: the contract close is 2026-09-28T07:00:00Z, matching the Summer practice copy that closed at its own season start, while the twin's 2-year horizon is the standard testing-area pattern; Run 3's reading requires trusting the count from a render while discarding the close date from that same render. So the 14-forecaster trickle rate is not this post's rate, and Run 3's 4.2 median is anchored too low. (2) Whether the Summer analog grew 156->180. Settled toward Run 2, which read q43339 directly as Closed with 156 forecasters and last comments dated May 17 2026; the 180 belongs to a separate testing-area EU-exit post (q43327) in Run 2's own project listing. So 156 is a final at-close figure, removing Run 3's evidence for ~3/day live accrual. Unsettled: this post's open date and current count - all three runs hit 403/auth walls, so the denominator carries real uncertainty (18-30 days) and I let the tails absorb it rather than pick a date by fiat. Pure judgment call, taken not split: the discrete-type discount is real and sizeable (the Summer batch's own by-type spread is 80 for discrete vs 180 for binary), so I sit below Runs 1-2's ~5.3 despite agreeing with their instrument reading, and well above Run 3 because its anchor post was the wrong one. Reference class and dispersion basis are my own, built from Run 2's by-type batch table, which was the only per-type evidence any run retrieved.
